prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to destroy chosen proteins, through PROTACs and the molecular-glue mechanism of thalidomide analogues

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part prize for targeted protein degradation to Crews, Deshaies and Handa. The round-1 exchange confirmed that this is the one topic on which members of very different backgrounds converge, and that the remaining dispute is about names and citation scope, not about the science. Event-driven, catalytic removal of a protein by induced proximity to an E3 ligase is a new pharmacological principle, it has been reproduced independently in many laboratories, and it reaches targets that occupancy-based inhibitors cannot. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the PROTAC concept. Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which is the mechanistic basis of the molecular-glue strand and the only degrader mechanism attached to approved drugs today. A citation that covers both strands describes the field as it actually is, and Crews, Deshaies and Handa are the three names whose contributions are each the origin of a distinct mechanism, not a refinement of one.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC has been approved, and a prize now rests on mechanism and breadth of confirmation, not on a finished clinical outcome. The three-name limit forces the exclusion of Ciulli, whose structure-guided VHL work made heterobifunctional degraders into a design discipline, and of Ito, Sakamoto, Kim and Gray. Choosing Handa over Ciulli is a judgement about which strand is more fundamental, and a committee that defines the achievement narrowly as heterobifunctional design would reasonably choose differently. The wider citation also risks reading as two achievements compressed into one. Sequencing (B014) remains the alternative with the cleanest maturity, but its credit across Solexa, 454 and other platforms is harder to settle than that of degradation.

responses.point: Aili proposes Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli for a PROTAC-only citation, argues the cereblon strand is a separate and earlier mechanistic discovery, and says he would accept Handa if glues are to be covered but wants Ciulli's absence discussed.
responses.response: I take his conditional seriously, and it narrows our difference to one question: is the glue mechanism inside the achievement. I think it is, because the thalidomide-cereblon mechanism is a degradation mechanism by induced proximity to an E3 ligase, and a prize that omits it leaves out the only strand with approved drugs. On Ciulli, I agree his absence needs to be stated openly. His work refined and made rational a design principle that Crews and Deshaies had already demonstrated, whereas the cereblon discovery created a mechanism that the PROTAC concept paper could not have supplied. I have not changed my view, but I regard his objection as the strongest argument against my trio, and I would find a Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli prize defensible if the committee decides the citation should be PROTAC-only.

responses.point: Linke, the chair, supports Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli with a PROTAC-focused citation, says he cannot dismiss Handa because two colleagues name him, and warns that the case is weaker than the ranking count suggests if PROTACs and glues cannot be separated.
responses.response: I agree that they cannot be cleanly separated, and I would draw the opposite conclusion from his: that inseparability argues for a citation that names both mechanisms and a name that represents the glue strand. The chair's question about a sole-part prize I answer yes: the lack of an approved PROTAC is a real timing risk, but I would still support B020 alone, because the mechanism is independently confirmed and the cereblon-based degraders already show clinical benefit. I also note his own two-name sequencing core of Balasubramanian and Klenerman. If B020 fails to reach a majority configuration, I would move to B014 with that core, and I would accept Rothberg's exclusion as a consequence of the three-name limit and a chemistry-centred citation.

responses.point: Aqvist backs Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli but concedes that a PROTAC-centred trio leaves out the cereblon glue strand, which he calls arguably the part with the most patient benefit, and suggests the prize might look rushed or incomplete without an approved degrader.
responses.response: His own concession is the reason I include Handa. If the glue strand has delivered the most patient benefit so far, a prize that omits it is the version most likely to look incomplete later, and including it also speaks to his worry about rushing, since it ties the citation to drugs already in use. I do not accept his suggestion that the Car-Parrinello method (B053) or Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B059) should reduce risk by being more mature, because they have almost no support beyond their advocates and B059 sits next to the 2010 cross-coupling prize. His restraint in not pressing B053 against the broad support for B020 seems right to me, and I regard it as consistent with my own handling of sequencing.

responses.point: Sparr proposes a two-part prize pairing Cullis for ionizable lipid nanoparticles with Crews and Deshaies for the PROTAC concept, arguing that the 2023 Medicine prize recognised nucleoside modification and not the carrier.
responses.response: Her argument that the carrier chemistry is distinct from nucleoside modification is fair, and the pKa tuning and phase behaviour are real chemistry, so I keep B049 as an alternative. I still prefer a single part, for two reasons. Her configuration spends two of three names on PROTACs and leaves the glue strand unrepresented, and one name for B049 is a thin account of a field she herself says was a team effort including industrial work. A two-part prize at three names gives each part a fragment, and I think the committee should not trade clarity of credit for breadth. If the committee does choose two parts, I would want the B049 name to be Cullis, as she proposes, and I would not extend it to others without a clearer account of who contributed which element.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a citation that covers both PROTACs and cereblon molecular glues, or require a PROTAC-only definition in which Ciulli is the natural third name
Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC drug makes the timing too early, given that cereblon-based degraders are already used in patients
Whether Handa alone can fairly represent the cereblon strand when Ito's contribution to the identification of cereblon is excluded by the name limit
Whether the sequencing credit could be settled on Balasubramanian and Klenerman if B020 fails to reach a majority configuration
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. My work on dNTP pools and ribonucleotide reductase is adjacent to the nucleotide chemistry in sequencing (B014), but I have no documented personal or institutional tie to any shortlisted candidate, including those credited under B020. My collaborators named in the profile are not candidates, so I do not see a need for recusal. This is unchanged from round 1.
